notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: White Matter Fibres of Cerebrum and Internal Capsule
notes.questionText: Classify white matter fibres of cerebrum with suitable examples. Add a note on fibres of internal capsule. (4+2)
notes.content:
##### Classification of White Matter Fibres
Cerebral white matter is organized into three major structural classes:
1. **Association Fibres:** Connect different cortical regions within the **same cerebral hemisphere**:
   * *Short association fibres:* Arcuate / "U-fibres" connecting adjacent gyri across a sulcus.
   * *Long association fibres:* Connect distant lobes (e.g., *Superior Longitudinal Fasciculus* connecting frontal and occipital lobes; *Arcuate Fasciculus* connecting Broca's and Wernicke's speech areas; *Cingulum*; *Uncinate Fasciculus* connecting frontal and temporal lobes).
2. **Commissural Fibres:** Interconnect homologous cortical regions of the **two opposite cerebral hemispheres**:
   * *Corpus Callosum:* The largest commissure (comprising rostrum, genu, body, and splenium).
   * *Anterior Commissure:* Connects olfactory structures and temporal lobes.
   * *Hippocampal Commissure (Commissure of Fornix):* Connects the two hippocampi.
   * *Habenular Commissure* and *Posterior Commissure*.
3. **Projection Fibres:** Interconnect the cerebral cortex with lower subcortical centers (diencephalon, brainstem, spinal cord) in both ascending and descending directions:
   * Radiate outward as the **corona radiata**, condense into the **internal capsule**, and continue into the **crus cerebri** of the midbrain.

##### Fibres of the Internal Capsule
A compact, V-shaped band of projection fibres flanked medially by the caudate nucleus and thalamus, and laterally by the lentiform nucleus.

```
                   ANTERIOR
                      |
              [ Head of Caudate ]
                   \     /
    ANTERIOR LIMB   \   /  <--- Frontopontine & Anterior Thalamic Radiations
                     \ /
                    GENU  <---- Corticonuclear (Corticobulbar) Tracts
                     / \
    POSTERIOR LIMB  /   \  <--- Corticospinal Tracts (Arm, Trunk, Leg)
                   /     \      & Superior Thalamic Radiations
           [ Thalamus ]   [ Lentiform Nucleus (Lateral) ]
                 |
     RETROLENTIFORM PART <----- Optic Radiations (to Area 17)
     SUBLENTIFORM PART   <----- Auditory Radiations (to Area 41, 42)
                      |
                   POSTERIOR
```

* **Subdivisions and Passing Tracts:**
  1. *Anterior Limb:* Frontopontine fibres; anterior thalamic radiation.
  2. *Genu:* **Corticonuclear (corticobulbar) tract** (motor control of cranial nerve motor nuclei).
  3. *Posterior Limb:*
     * Anterior two-thirds: **Corticospinal tract** (arranged somatotopically: Arm, Trunk, Leg from anterior to posterior).
     * Posterior one-third: Superior thalamic radiation (third-order general sensory fibres from VPL/VPM nuclei to sensory cortex).
  4. *Retrolentiform Part:* **Optic radiation** (posterior thalamic radiation from lateral geniculate body to primary visual cortex).
  5. *Sublentiform Part:* **Auditory radiation** (from medial geniculate body to primary auditory cortex).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Formation of Placenta and Placental Barrier
notes.questionText: Describe the formation of placenta. Add a note on placental barrier. (4+2)
notes.content:
##### Formation of Placenta
* The placenta is a temporary fetomaternal organ facilitating metabolic, gas, and endocrine exchange:
  1. **Fetal Component (Chorion Frondosum):** Derived from the trophoblast and extraembryonic somatic mesoderm. Primary, secondary, and tertiary chorionic villi proliferate extensively at the embryonic pole abutting the decidua basalis, forming the bushy *chorion frondosum* [111001:Q01].
  2. **Maternal Component (Decidua Basalis):** Derived from the functional layer of the gravid endometrium underlying the site of implantation [111001:Q01].
* **Full-Term Morphology:** Discoid mass, diameter $15–20\text{ cm}$, thickness $2.5\text{ cm}$, weight $\approx 500\text{ g}$.
  * *Fetal Surface:* Smooth, covered by translucent amnion; insertion of the umbilical cord with radiating umbilical vessels.
  * *Maternal Surface:* Rough, divided by decidual septa into 15–20 polygonal lobes (**cotyledons**).

##### Placental Barrier (Placental Membrane)
The composite tissue membrane intervening between fetal intracapillary blood and maternal blood circulating in the intervillous spaces:
* **Components in Early Pregnancy (4 layers):**
  1. Syncytiotrophoblast (outer multinucleated layer)
  2. Cytotrophoblast (inner cellular layer of Langhans)
  3. Extraembryonic mesodermal connective tissue core
  4. Endothelium of fetal capillary with its basal lamina
* **Components at Full Term (Late Pregnancy - 2 layers):**
  * The cytotrophoblast and continuous mesodermal stroma regress, leaving an extremely thin barrier ($2–4\ \mu\text{m}$) consisting solely of:
    1. **Syncytiotrophoblast**
    2. **Fetal capillary endothelium** (with fused basement membranes)
  * Maximizes diffusive transport of oxygen and nutrients while retaining maternal IgG transmission.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Cervical Lymph Nodes and Lymph Node Microscopy
notes.questionText: Describe the location, drainage and applied anatomy of cervical lymphnodes. Add a note on microscopy of lymphnode. (4+2)
notes.content:
##### Location and Drainage of Cervical Lymph Nodes
* **Superficial Cervical Nodes:** Clustered along the external jugular vein superficial to the sternocleidomastoid; drain superficial structures of the ear and lower face.
* **Deep Cervical Chain:** Form a vertical chain embedded along the carotid sheath and internal jugular vein:
  * Divided by the intermediate tendon of the omohyoid into:
    1. **Superior Deep Cervical Nodes:** Located above omohyoid. Includes the prominent **Jugulodigastric Node** (Wood's node; lies below posterior belly of digastric, drains the palatine tonsil; primary node enlarged in tonsillitis).
    2. **Inferior Deep Cervical Nodes:** Located below omohyoid. Includes the **Jugulo-omohyoid Node** (drains tongue lymphatics directly) and **Supraclavicular (Virchow's) Nodes**.
* **Clinical Drainage Levels (Levels I–VI):**
  * Level I: Submental and Submandibular
  * Level II: Upper deep cervical (jugulodigastric)
  * Level III: Middle deep cervical
  * Level IV: Lower deep cervical (jugulo-omohyoid)
  * Level V: Posterior triangle nodes (along spinal accessory nerve)
  * Level VI: Anterior compartment (prelaryngeal, pretracheal, paratracheal)
* **Microscopy of Lymph Node:**
  * **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:101001:Q08]]` under *Anatomy — Paper I — 2025_JANUARY* for detailed histological architecture (capsule, subcapsular sinus, cortex with follicles, paracortex, medullary cords/sinuses).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: External Jugular Vein — Formation, Course, Termination, and Tributaries
notes.questionText: Describe the formation, course, termination and tributaries of external jugular vein.
notes.content:
* **Formation:** Formed behind the angle of the mandible by the confluence of the **Posterior Auricular Vein** and the **Posterior Division of the Retromandibular Vein**.
* **Course:**
  * Descends vertically across the superficial surface of the **Sternocleidomastoid** muscle, running obliquely downward and backward embedded in superficial fascia.
  * Pierces the investing layer of deep cervical fascia $\approx 2.5\text{ cm}$ above the clavicle at the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid.
* **Termination:** Empties directly into the **Subclavian Vein**.
* **Tributaries:**
  1. Posterior external jugular vein
  2. Transverse cervical vein
  3. Suprascapular vein
  4. Anterior jugular vein

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Principles of Genetic Counselling
notes.questionText: Describe the principle of genetic counselling.
notes.content:
* **Definition:** A non-directive communication process dealing with human problems associated with the occurrence or risk of recurrence of a genetic disorder in a family.
* **Core Principles:**
  1. *Diagnostic Accuracy:* Confirming phenotypic diagnosis using detailed family pedigree analysis (minimum 3 generations), karyotyping, and molecular tests.
  2. *Risk Estimation:* Calculating precise mathematical recurrence risk (e.g., 50% for autosomal dominant, 25% for autosomal recessive).
  3. *Non-Directive Counselling:* Providing objective, unbiased facts and reproductive options (prenatal diagnosis, assisted reproduction) without dictating choices.
  4. *Autonomy & Informed Consent:* Upholding parental decision-making authority regarding pregnancy continuation or termination.
  5. *Confidentiality & Emotional Support:* Protecting private genetic information and offering psychologic guidance.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Structural and Functional Differences Between Elastic and Muscular Arteries
notes.questionText: Explain the structural and functional differences between elastic and muscular arteries.
notes.content:
| Feature | Elastic (Conducting) Arteries | Muscular (Distributing) Arteries |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Examples** | Aorta, Brachiocephalic, Common Carotid, Subclavian | Brachial, Radial, Femoral, Popliteal, Coronary |
| **Tunica Intima** | Relatively thick; internal elastic lamina is poorly demarcated (blends with media) | Well-defined with a prominent, undulating, scalloped **Internal Elastic Lamina (IEL)** |
| **Tunica Media** | Massive; composed predominantly of **40–70 concentric fenestrated elastic laminae** with sparse smooth muscle | Thick; dominated by **up to 40 concentric layers of circularly arranged smooth muscle cells**; few elastic fibers |
| **External Elastic Lamina**| Indistinct | Distinct, separating media from adventitia |
| **Primary Function** | **Windkessel Effect:** Expands during systole to store stroke volume and recoils during diastole to maintain continuous peripheral perfusion | **Vasoregulation:** Contracts (vasoconstriction) and relaxes (vasodilation) to regulate regional blood flow and systemic vascular resistance |

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Correct Procedure While Handling Cadavers
notes.questionText: Describe the correct procedure while handling cadavers.
notes.content:
* **Respect and Demeanor:** The cadaver represents a deceased human donor; quiet, dignified, and solemn behavior must be maintained in the dissection hall at all times.
* **Prohibition of Recording:** Complete ban on taking photographs, selfies, or videos; strictly no sharing of images on social media platforms or outside educational rooms [112001:Q24].
* **Preservation & Tissue Care:**
  * Keep dissected specimens and organs moist by routinely applying wetting solution (formalin/glycerol-water sprays).
  * Cover specimens with damp cloths and secure the body bag or tank lid tightly after every dissection session to prevent desiccation.
* **Instrument Discipline:** Avoid resting heavy textbooks, instruments, or elbows directly on the cadaver's body [112001:Q24].
* **Waste Disposal:** Any discarded tissue, fascia, or fat must be placed strictly in color-coded clinical waste containers (**Yellow Bins** for human anatomical waste) for scheduled respectful cremation or burial [112001:Q01].

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Acute Appendicitis Case — Vermiform Appendix
notes.questionText: A 14-year-old girl was brought to the hospital with complaints of fever, vomiting and acute pain around umbilicus. On examination, the surgeon found that she was having maximum tenderness at Mc Burney’s point. From the history and examination, he came to the diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Based on your anatomical knowledge, answer the following questions. a) Why is pain felt around umbilicus b) Where is Mc Burney’s point c) What are the various positions of vermiform appendix d) Briefly describe the blood supply, development and microscopy of vermiform appendix (1+1+3+5)
notes.content:
##### a) Why Pain is Felt Around Umbilicus
* The vermiform appendix is embryologically derived from the **midgut**.
* Visceral sensory afferent fibers conducting pain from the appendix accompany sympathetic vasomotor nerves back to the **T10 spinal cord segment**.
* The **T10 somatic dermatome** maps to the skin surrounding the **umbilicus**. Consequently, referred visceral appendiceal pain is initially perceived in the periumbilical region.
* Later, when inflammatory exudate reaches the parietal peritoneum, somatic pain localizes precisely to the right iliac fossa (McBurney’s point).

##### b) McBurney’s Point
* **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:102001:Q01]]` (subpart c) under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2025_JANUARY* for surface marking and anatomical significance.

##### c) Positions of Vermiform Appendix
* **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:102001:Q01]]` (subpart b) under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2025_JANUARY* for 12 o’clock (retrocecal), 4 o’clock (pelvic), subcecal, and pre-/post-ileal clock-face distribution.

##### d) Blood Supply, Development, and Microscopy of Appendix
* **Blood Supply:** Appendicular artery (from inferior division of ileocolic artery); travels in the free border of the mesoappendix; is an anatomical end-artery [102001:Q01].
* **Development:** Arises in the 6th week as a rapid distal elongation of the cecal diverticulum arising from the antimesenteric border of the caudal limb of the primitive midgut loop.
* **Microscopy:** Simple columnar epithelium lining mucosal crypts; lamina propria and submucosa are packed with **massive confluent lymphoid aggregations/follicles with germinal centers** [102001:Q01].

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Interior of Right Atrium and Its Development
notes.questionText: Describe the features of the interior of the right atrium. Add a note on its development (4+2)
notes.content:
##### Interior of Right Atrium
Divided into two distinct developmental compartments separated internally by the vertical muscular ridge, the **Crista Terminalis** (corresponding to the *sulcus terminalis* externally):

```
                   Superior Vena Cava
                           |
             +-------------+-------------+
             | ANTERIOR / ROUGH PART     | POSTERIOR / SMOOTH PART
             | (Musculi Pectinati)       | (Sinus Venarum)
             |                           | - SVC Orifice (no valve)
             | - Right Auricle           | - IVC Orifice (Eustachian valve)
             |                           | - Coronary Sinus Orifice
             |             [ CRISTA      |   (Thebesian valve)
             |           TERMINALIS ]    | - Fossa Ovalis & Limbus
             +-------------+-------------+
                           |
                   Right AV Orifice
                   (Tricuspid Valve)
```

1. **Posterior Smooth Part (Sinus Venarum):**
   * Smooth, thin walls; receives systemic venous return:
   * *SVC Orifice:* Opens into posterosuperior aspect; valveless.
   * *IVC Orifice:* Opens inferoposteriorly; guarded by the rudiment **Valve of IVC (Eustachian valve)** [112001:Q23].
   * *Coronary Sinus Orifice:* Situated between IVC opening and AV orifice; guarded by the **Valve of Coronary Sinus (Thebesian valve)**.
   * *Foramina Venarum Minimarum:* Punctate openings of thebesian veins.
2. **Anterior Rough Part (Pectinate Part & Right Auricle):**
   * Characterized by parallel horizontal muscular ridges resembling teeth of a comb, the **Musculi Pectinati**, which originate at right angles from the crista terminalis.
3. **Interatrial Septum:**
   * Features the **Fossa Ovalis** (oval floor formed by embryonic septum primum) and **Limbus Fossa Ovalis** (prominent crescentic upper margin formed by septum secundum) [101001:Q09, 112001:Q23].
4. **Triangle of Koch:** Boundaries: Base of septal cusp of tricuspid valve, Tendon of Todaro, and orifice of coronary sinus. Lodges the **Atrioventricular (AV) Node**.

##### Development of Right Atrium
* The posterior smooth part develops from the **absorption of the right horn of the sinus venosus**.
* The anterior pectinate part develops from the **primitive right atrium**.
* The crista terminalis represents the line of embryonic fusion between the primitive atrium and the sinus venosus (right venous valve).

Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) [102001:Q05]
2. Terminal branches of Right Phrenic Nerve
3. Lymphatic channels | | **Esophageal Opening** | **T10** | Muscular fibers of the Right Crus | 1. Esophagus
2. Anterior and Posterior Vagal Trunks

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Extrahepatic Biliary Apparatus
notes.questionText: Describe the gross features and relations of components of extrahepatic biliary apparatus.
notes.content:
Comprises the gallbladder, right and left hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct, cystic duct, and common bile duct:

```
        Right & Left Hepatic Ducts
                    \      /
              Common Hepatic Duct     Gallbladder
                       \                  /
                        \            Cystic Duct (Spiral Valve of Heister)
                         \              /
                          v            v
                         COMMON BILE DUCT (CBD)
                                |
             +------------------+------------------+
             | 1. Supraduodenal: In lesser omentum |
             | 2. Retroduodenal: Behind 1st part   |
             | 3. Infraduodenal: In head pancreas  |
             | 4. Intraduodenal: Ampulla of Vater  |
             +------------------+------------------+
                                |
                                v
                      Major Duodenal Papilla (D2)
```

* **Gross Features & Relations of Parts:**
  1. **Gallbladder:**
     * **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:102001:Q07]]` under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2025_JULY*.
  2. **Cystic Duct:** $3–4\text{ cm}$ long; mucosa contains the **spiral fold (Valve of Heister)** keeping the lumen patent. Forms the lower boundary of **Calot’s Triangle** (bounded medially by common hepatic duct, superiorly by inferior liver border; contains cystic artery).
  3. **Common Bile Duct (CBD):** Length $\approx 7.5\text{ cm}$; divided into 4 parts:
     * *Supraduodenal Part:* Runs in the right free border of the lesser omentum anterior to the portal vein and to the right of the hepatic artery.
     * *Retroduodenal Part:* Descends behind the 1st part of duodenum with IVC behind it.
     * *Infraduodenal Part:* Embedded in a groove on the posterior surface of the head of pancreas.
     * *Intraduodenal Part:* Pierces the posteromedial wall of the 2nd part of duodenum obliquely, uniting with the main pancreatic duct to form the **Ampulla of Vater**, opening on the **major duodenal papilla** guarded by the **Sphincter of Oddi**.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Microanatomy of Kidney and Juxtaglomerular Apparatus
notes.questionText: Describe the microanatomy of the kidney. What are the components of the juxtaglomerular apparatus (4+2)
notes.content:
##### Microanatomy of Kidney
* **Nephron (Structural and Functional Unit):**
  1. **Renal (Malpighian) Corpuscle:**
     * *Glomerulus:* Anastomosing network of fenestrated capillary loops derived from afferent arteriole, converging into efferent arteriole.
     * *Bowman's Capsule:* Double-walled cup; parietal layer is simple squamous; visceral layer consists of specialized **Podocytes** possessing primary and secondary pedicels (foot processes) creating **filtration slits** bridged by slit diaphragms.
     * *Filtration Barrier:* Fenestrated endothelium[[KUHS-QUESTION:112001:Q20]]
#### Short Essay: Microanatomy of Kidney and Juxtaglomerular Apparatus *(Continued)*

##### Microanatomy of Kidney
* **Nephron (Structural and Functional Unit):**
  1. **Renal (Malpighian) Corpuscle:**
     * *Glomerulus:* Anastomosing network of fenestrated capillary loops derived from the afferent arteriole, converging into the efferent arteriole.
     * *Bowman's Capsule:* Double-walled epithelial cup; parietal layer consists of simple squamous epithelium; visceral layer consists of specialized **Podocytes** possessing primary and secondary pedicels (foot processes) creating **filtration slits** bridged by slit diaphragms.
     * *Filtration Barrier (Trilaminar):*
       1. Fenestrated capillary endothelium (pores $70–90\text{ nm}$).
       2. Fused glomerular basement membrane (GBM, rich in negatively charged heparan sulfate).
       3. Slit diaphragms between podocyte foot processes ($25–30\text{ nm}$).
  2. **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT):**
     * Lined by **simple cuboidal to low columnar epithelium** with an extensive apical **brush border of tall microvilli** [112001:Q01].
     * Abundant basolateral invaginations packed with vertical mitochondria (acidophilic cytoplasm); active reabsorption of 65–70% of filtrate.
  3. **Loop of Henle:**
     * *Thick Descending & Ascending Limbs:* Simple cuboidal epithelium.
     * *Thin Descending & Ascending Segments:* Simple squamous epithelium.
  4. **Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT):**
     * Lined by **simple cuboidal epithelium** lacking a brush border (clean, wide lumen); cells have distinct lateral cell boundaries.

```
       Afferent Arteriole          Efferent Arteriole
               \                     /
         [ JUXTAGLOMERULAR CELLS ]  /
                 \                 /
                  v               v
               +---------------------+
               |   GLOMERULUS        |  <--- Fenestrated Capillaries
               |  (Visceral Podocyte |
               |        Layer)       |
               +---------------------+
                         |
                 Bowman's Space
                         |
                  PCT (Brush Border)
                         |
                  Loop of Henle
                         |
               DCT (Macula Densa sits at vascular pole)
```

##### Components of the Juxtaglomerular Apparatus (JGA)
Located at the vascular pole of each nephron where the DCT touches its parent afferent arteriole:
1. **Juxtaglomerular (JG) Cells:**
   * Modified, rounded, myoepithelial smooth muscle cells situated in the wall of the **afferent arteriole**.
   * Contain secretory zymogen granules of **Renin** (baroreceptor sensing perfusion pressure).
2. **Macula Densa:**
   * Specialized tall, crowded, narrow columnar epithelial cells with closely packed dark nuclei in the wall of the **terminal straight/DCT**.
   * Acts as a **chemoreceptor** monitoring luminal $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ concentrations.
3. **Lacis Cells (Extraglomerular Mesangial / Polkissen Cells):**
   * Flat, pale-staining cells occupying the triangular space between afferent and efferent arterioles and macula densa; play an intermediary signaling role.
* **Diagram Reference:** [Kidney Nephron Diagram (Wikimedia Commons)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/03/Kidney_multilingual.svg)

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Anatomical Basis of Ischemic Heart Disease (IHD)
notes.questionText: Describe the anatomical basis of ischemic heart disease.
notes.content:
* **Functional End-Arteries:** Coronary arteries are physiological and functional end-arteries; the microscopic anastomoses between LAD, LCx, and RCA are inadequate to supply myocardium if sudden acute occlusion occurs.
* **Atherosclerotic Predilection Sites:**
  1. *LAD (Left Anterior Descending):* Most common site ("widow maker"); occludes anterior wall of LV and anterior two-thirds of IV septum [101001:Q01].
  2. *RCA (Right Coronary Artery):* Occlusion causes inferior/diaphragmatic wall infarction and AV nodal blocks.
  3. *LCx (Left Circumflex Artery):* Lateral wall infarction.
* **Referred Cardiac Pain (Angina Pectoris):**
  * Myocardial ischemia generates lactic acid, stimulating sensory free nerve endings.
  * Visceral sympathetic afferents travel via cardiac nerves back to **T1–T5 spinal segments**.
  * Somatosensory cross-talk in the dorsal horn refers pain to the precordium, medial aspect of the left arm and forearm (T1 dermatome, via intercostobrachial nerve), and neck/jaw.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Lumbar Puncture — Site and Structures Pierced
notes.questionText: Describe the site and structures pierced while performing a lumbar puncture
notes.content:
* **Optimal Anatomical Site:**
  * Performed at the **L3–L4** or **L4–L5 intervertebral space** [111001:Q01].
  * *Landmark (Tuffier’s Line):* The horizontal line connecting the highest points of the **iliac crests** crosses the spine of the L4 vertebra.
  * Safe because the adult spinal cord terminates at the lower border of **L1** (L3 in infants) [102001:Q06], while the subarachnoid space (lumbar cistern) extends to **S2** [111001:Q01].

```
  Skin -> Superficial Fascia -> Supraspinous Lig. -> Interspinous Lig.
  -> Ligamentum Flavum -> Epidural Space -> Dura Mater -> Arachnoid Mater
  -> Subarachnoid Space (CSF)
```

* **Structures Pierced (Superficial to Deep):**
  1. Skin
  2. Superficial fascia (fat and Camper's/Scarpa's fascia)
  3. Supraspinous ligament
  4. Interspinous ligament
  5. **Ligamentum flavum** (gives a characteristic sudden "pop" or loss of resistance)
  6. Epidural space (containing internal vertebral venous plexus and fat)
  7. **Dura mater** (gives second minor "give")
  8. **Arachnoid mater**
  9. Enters the **Subarachnoid space (Lumbar Cistern)** to aspirate CSF.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Dissection Hall Ethics Reflection
notes.questionText: Reflect on the following scenarios in the dissection hall: i) Placing anatomy books and dissection instruments on the cadaver ii) Taking pictures of tablemates around the cadaver table and uploading them on social media (2+2)
notes.content:
* **Scenario i: Placing books and instruments on the cadaver:**
  * *Reflection:* The cadaver must never be treated as an inanimate table or workbench. Placing books, bags, or surgical trays directly on a donor’s body violates bodily integrity and diminishes moral solemnity. Respectful practice requires using adjacent instrument trays and book stands, recognizing that human tissue deserves honor [111001:Q24].
* **Scenario ii: Taking pictures and uploading on social media:**
  * *Reflection:* Taking photographs or posting images/videos of dissection on social media is a severe breach of medical ethics, confidentiality, and institutional conduct rules [111001:Q24]. It exploits altruistic body donors who consented solely to medical education, and risks destroying public trust in anatomical donation programs.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Arches of Foot and Flat Foot
notes.questionText: A 20-year-old male had applied for selection into defence academy in India. His application was rejected during physical examination on the grounds of Bilateral Flat Foot. a) What is the anatomical basis of flat foot. b) Classify arches of foot. c) What are the components and features of each type of arches of foot. d) What are the factors that maintain the arches of foot (2+2+6+5)
notes.content:
##### a) Anatomical Basis of Flat Foot (Pes Planus)
* Occurs when the medial longitudinal arch collapses, causing the medial border of the sole to touch the ground.
* **Causes:** Laxity or rupture of the **plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament**, paralysis or dysfunction of the **Tibialis Posterior tendon** (loss of dynamic sling), or prolonged standing on rigid unyielding footwear.

##### b) Classification of Arches of Foot
1. **Longitudinal Arches:**
   * Medial Longitudinal Arch (higher, resilient, shock-absorbing).
   * Lateral Longitudinal Arch (lower, rigid, transmits body weight to ground).
2. **Transverse Arch:**
   * Anterior Transverse Arch (complete; across metatarsal heads).
   * Posterior Transverse Arch (half-dome across cuboid and 3 cuneiforms).

##### c) Components and Features of Each Arch

| Arch | Posterior Pillar | Summit | Anterior Pillar | Keystone |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Medial Longitudinal Arch** | Medial tubercle of calcaneus | Superior articular surface of talus | Heads of 1st, 2nd, 3rd metatarsals | **Head of Talus** [101001:Q14] |
| **Lateral Longitudinal Arch**| Lateral tubercle of calcaneus | Subtalar articular surface of calcaneus | Heads of 4th and 5th metatarsals | **Cuboid Bone** |

##### d) Factors Maintaining Arches
1. **Shape of Bones (Bony Architecture):** Wedge-shaped tarsals fitting together like stones in an architectural stone arch (especially cuneiforms in transverse arch).
2. **Staples (Intersegmental Ligaments):** Short, strong ligaments binding adjacent bone bases (Spring ligament for medial arch; Long & Short plantar ligaments for lateral arch).
3. **Tie-Beams:** Structures connecting the anterior and posterior pillars:
   * **Plantar Aponeurosis** (crucial tie-beam).
   * Abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis.
4. **Slings (Suspension Cables):** Tendons looping under the arches from above:
   * *Medial Arch:* **Tibialis posterior** and **Tibialis anterior**.
   * *Lateral & Transverse Arch:* **Peroneus longus** [112001:Q01].

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Femoral Nerve
notes.content:
* **Origin & Root Value:** Largest branch of the Lumbar Plexus; arises from the dorsal divisions of the ventral rami of **L2, L3, L4**.
* **Course:**
  * Emerges through the lateral border of Psoas major.
  * Descends in the groove between Psoas major and Iliacus, passing behind the inguinal ligament lateral to the femoral sheath and femoral artery.
  * Enters the femoral triangle and divides $\approx 2.5\text{ cm}$ below the inguinal ligament into anterior and posterior divisions.
* **Branches:**
  * *Anterior Division:*
    * Muscular: **Sartorius** and **Pectineus**.
    * Cutaneous: **Intermediate cutaneous nerve of thigh** and **Medial cutaneous nerve of thigh**.
  * *Posterior Division:*
    * Muscular: **Quadriceps femoris** (Rectus femoris [112001:Q24], Vastus lateralis, Vastus medialis, Vastus intermedius) and Articularis genu.
    * Cutaneous: **Saphenous Nerve** (longest cutaneous branch; accompanies femoral vessels in adductor canal [101001:Q12], descends down medial leg with great saphenous vein).
    * Articular: Hip joint (from nerve to rectus femoris) and Knee joint (from nerves to vasti).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Radial Nerve and Saturday Night Palsy
notes.questionText: Radial nerve- root value, course and branches in axilla, arm and cubital fossa. What is Saturday night palsy.
notes.content:
* **Root Value:** **C5, C6, C7, C8, T1** (from posterior cord of brachial plexus) [101001:Q11].
* **Course and Branches:**
  * *Axilla:* Descends posterior to axillary artery; gives branches to long and medial heads of triceps and posterior cutaneous nerve of arm.
  * *Arm:* Passes inferolaterally through the lower triangular space into the **radial (spiral) groove** between lateral and medial heads of triceps accompanied by profunda brachii artery [101001:Q10]. Supplies lateral and medial heads of triceps, anconeus, lower lateral cutaneous nerve of arm, posterior cutaneous nerve of forearm.
  * *Cubital Fossa:* Pierces lateral intermuscular septum to enter anterior compartment between brachialis and brachioradialis [111001:Q01]. Supplies brachioradialis and ECRL.
  * *Termination:* At lateral epicondyle, divides into **Superficial Radial Nerve** (sensory) and **Deep Branch (Posterior Interosseous Nerve)** which pierces supinator to supply extensor muscles of forearm.
* **Saturday Night Palsy:** Acute radial nerve compression against the mid-shaft of the humerus caused by falling asleep with the arm draped over a hard chair (often intoxicated); presents as temporary neuropraxia with **wrist drop** and numbness over the anatomical snuffbox [111001:Q18].

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Serratus Anterior Muscle
notes.content:
* **Origin:** Arises by 8 fleshy digitations from the outer surfaces of the upper 8 ribs.
* **Insertion:** Costal surface of the medial border of the scapula:
  * 1st digitation to superior angle.
  * Next 2 digitations to medial border.
  * Lower 5 digitations converge onto the **inferior angle of scapula**.
* **Nerve Supply:** **Long Thoracic Nerve (Nerve of Bell)** (root value **C5, C6, C7**).
* **Actions:**
  * **Protraction of Scapula:** Pulls scapula forward around chest wall ("boxer's muscle").
  * **Hyperabduction:** Rotates the inferior angle of the scapula upward and laterally, tilting the glenoid cavity upward to permit abduction above $90^\circ$ [111001:Q08].
  * Fixes scapula against thoracic cage.
* **Clinical Anatomy:** Injury to the long thoracic nerve causes **Winged Scapula** (medial border and inferior angle project backward when pushing against a wall).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Types of Epiphysis
notes.content:
1. **Pressure Epiphysis:** Articular end of a long bone that transmits body weight; subjected to pressure; protects the growth plate (e.g., Head of femur, lower end of radius, condyles of tibia).
2. **Traction Epiphysis:** Non-articular bony projection produced by the pull of a muscular tendon; ossifies later than pressure epiphyses (e.g., Greater and lesser trochanters of femur, tubercles of humerus).
3. **Atavistic Epiphysis:** Phylogenetically represents an independent bone that became fused with another bone in humans (e.g., Coracoid process of scapula, os trigonum).
4. **Aberrant Epiphysis:** Epiphysis that is not consistently present, seen at atypical sites (e.g., Head of 1st metacarpal bone).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Histology of Thin Skin and Appendages
notes.questionText: Histology of thin skin. Write a note on appendages of skin.
notes.content:
* **Histology of Thin Skin:** Covers most of the body; possesses thin stratum corneum, lacks stratum lucidum [101001:Q11], possesses hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and sweat glands:
  * *Epidermis:* Stratum basale, spinosum, granulosum, corneum.
  * *Dermis:* Papillary layer (loose areolar tissue with Meissner's corpuscles) and Reticular layer (dense irregular collagenous tissue).
* **Appendages of Skin:**
  1. *Hair Follicles:* Invaginations of epidermis associated with **Arrector pili smooth muscles**.
  2. *Sebaceous Glands:* Holocrine branched acinar glands secreting lipid sebum into hair follicles.
  3. *Eccrine Sweat Glands:* Merocrine coiled simple tubular glands for thermoregulation.
  4. *Apocrine Sweat Glands:* Located in axilla/areola/perineum; secrete viscous pheromonal fluid.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Microscopic Structure of Thymus
notes.content:
* **Capsule and Lobules:** Surrounded by a thin fibrocollagenous capsule; incomplete interlobular septa divide parenchyma into incomplete thymic lobules.
* **Cortex (Outer Dark Zone):** Packed densely with actively proliferating immature **T-lymphocytes (thymocytes)**, macrophages, and cortical epithelial reticular cells; presence of blood-thymus barrier.
* **Medulla (Inner Pale Zone):** Continuous between adjacent lobules; contains mature T-cells, dendritic cells, and **Hassall's (Thymic) Corpuscles**:
  * *Hassall’s Corpuscles:* Eosinophilic, concentric onion-skin rings of degenerate flattened epithelial reticular cells; diagnostic hallmark of thymus.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Coronary Sinus
notes.content:
* **Location:** Lies in the posterior part of the coronary sulcus (atrioventricular groove) between the left atrium and left ventricle.
* **Termination:** Empties into the **posteroinferior wall of the Right Atrium** between the IVC opening and tricuspid orifice; opening is guarded by the **Valve of Coronary Sinus (Thebesian valve)** [112001:Q15].
* **Tributaries:**
  1. *Great Cardiac Vein:* Accompanies LAD, ascends to enter left end of sinus.
  2. *Middle Cardiac Vein:* Runs in posterior interventricular groove.
  3. *Small Cardiac Vein:* Accompanies marginal branch of RCA.
  4. *Posterior Vein of Left Ventricle.*
  5. *Oblique Vein of Left Atrium (Vein of Marshall):* Remnant of embryonic left common cardinal vein.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Inguinal Canal and Inguinal Hernia
notes.questionText: A 65-year-old man with chronic history of cough and consti pation complained he noticed a gradually increasing swelling in the right groin and feels a dragging sensation at that site. On examination, it was noticed a globular swelling above the pubic tubercle which increased in size on coughing . The patient was diagnosed to have Inguinal hernia a) Based on the anatomical knowledge, what are the reasons for swellings in the groin region b) What are the boundaries of Inguinal canal c) What are the contents of Inguinal canal d) What are factors which maintain the Integrity of Inguinal canal e) What is Hesselbach’s triangle (2+5+2+3+3)
notes.content:
##### a) Reasons for Swellings in Groin Region
1. Inguinal Hernia (Indirect or Direct)
2. Femoral Hernia [112001:Q10]
3. Saphena Varix (dilation of upper great saphenous vein)
4. Inguinal Lymphadenopathy
5. Undescended Testis / Hydrocele of spermatic cord or canal of Nuck
6. Psoas Abscess pointing below inguinal ligament

##### b) Boundaries of Inguinal Canal
An oblique intermuscular tunnel $\approx 4\text{ cm}$ long directed downwards, forwards, and medially above the medial half of the inguinal ligament [112001:Q04]:
* **Anterior Wall:** External oblique aponeurosis along the whole length; reinforced in lateral third by fleshy fibers of internal oblique.
* **Posterior Wall:** Fascia transversalis along the whole length [112001:Q01]; reinforced in medial third by the **Conjoint Tendon** [112001:Q01] and reflected ligament.
* **Roof:** Arching lower fleshy fibers of **Internal Oblique** and **Transversus Abdominis**.
* **Floor:** Grooved upper surface of the **Inguinal Ligament** (Poupart’s); medially reinforced by the lacunar ligament (Gimbernat's) [112001:Q04].
* **Deep Inguinal Ring:** Oval aperture in **fascia transversalis** $1.25\text{ cm}$ above mid-inguinal point, lateral to inferior epigastric artery.
* **Superficial Inguinal Ring:** Triangular gap in **external oblique aponeurosis** above the pubic crest.

##### c) Contents of Inguinal Canal
1. **Spermatic Cord** in males (containing ductus deferens, testicular artery, pampiniform venous plexus, cremasteric artery, artery to vas, genital branch of genitofemoral nerve, testicular lymphatics) [112001:Q01].
2. **Round Ligament of Uterus** in females [112001:Q01].
3. **Ilioinguinal Nerve** (enters canal through its lateral wall; does not pass through deep ring, exits via superficial ring) [112001:Q01].

##### d) Factors Maintaining Integrity of Inguinal Canal
1. *Flap-Valve Mechanism:* Obliquity of canal ensures increased intra-abdominal pressure presses anterior and posterior walls together.
2. *Shutter Mechanism of Keith:* Contraction of arching fibers of internal oblique and transversus abdominis pulls roof down to floor.
3. *Ball-Valve Action:* Cremaster muscle contracts, plugging superficial ring with spermatic cord.
4. *Reinforcement:* Strong conjoint tendon opposes weak superficial ring behind; fleshy internal oblique covers deep ring in front.

##### e) Hesselbach’s Triangle
* **Boundaries:**
  * *Medial:* Lateral border of Rectus Abdominis muscle.
  * *Lateral:* **Inferior Epigastric Artery**.
  * *Inferior (Base):* **Inguinal Ligament**.
* Divided by medial umbilical fold into medial and lateral inguinal fossae [112001:Q01]; site through which **direct inguinal hernias** protrude.
* **Diagram Reference:** [Inguinal Canal & Rings (Wikimedia Commons)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b4/Gray1227.png)

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Cavernous Sinus
notes.questionText: Classify the dural venous s inuses. Describe the c avernous sinus under the following headings- a) Position b) Relations c) Tributaries and communications d) Applied anatomy (3+1+5+4+2)
notes.content:
##### Classification of Dural Venous Sinuses
* **Paired Sinuses (6):** Cavernous, Superior petrosal, Inferior petrosal, Transverse, Sigmoid, Sphenoparietal sinuses.
* **Unpaired Sinuses (6):** Superior sagittal, Inferior sagittal, Straight, Occipital, Anterior and Posterior intercavernous sinuses.

##### Cavernous Sinus Anatomy
* **a) Position:** Large bilaterally paired trabeculated dural venous spaces located on the body of the sphenoid bone on either side of the sella turcica in the middle cranial fossa; extends from the superior orbital fissure to the apex of the petrous temporal bone [111001:Q01].
* **b) Relations:**
  * *Medial:* Pituitary gland (hypophysis cerebri) and sphenoidal air sinuses.
  * *Lateral:* Temporal lobe of cerebral hemisphere and uncus.
  * *Superior:* Internal carotid artery (after emerging) and optic tract.
  * *Structures in Lateral Wall (from Superior to Inferior):*
    1. **Oculomotor Nerve (CN III)**
    2. **Trochlear Nerve (CN IV)**
    3. **Ophthalmic Nerve (V1)**
    4. **Maxillary Nerve (V2)**
  * *Structures Passing Through the Center of the Sinus (Bathed in Blood):*
    1. **Internal Carotid Artery** (with sympathetic plexus)
    2. **Abducens Nerve (CN VI)** (most vulnerable to intracavernous pathology)

```
                       SELLAR CAVITY (Pituitary Gland)
                                    |
          +-------------------------+-------------------------+
          |  LATERAL WALL           |  INTERNAL CONTENTS      |
          |  - Oculomotor (CN III)  |  - Internal Carotid A.  |
          |  - Trochlear (CN IV)    |  - Abducens Nerve (VI)  |
          |  - Ophthalmic (CN V1)   |                         |
          |  - Maxillary (CN V2)    |                         |
          +-------------------------+-------------------------+
```

* **c) Tributaries and Communications:**
  * *Tributaries:* Superior and inferior ophthalmic veins, superficial middle cerebral vein, sphenoparietal sinus, central vein of retina.
  * *Drainage:* Via superior petrosal sinus to transverse sinus, and inferior petrosal sinus to internal jugular vein.
  * *Communications:* With opposite sinus via intercavernous sinuses; with pterygoid venous plexus via emissary veins passing through foramen ovale and spinosum [102001:Q11]; with facial vein via superior ophthalmic vein.
* **d) Applied Anatomy:**
  * **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:111001:Q17]]` under *Anatomy — Paper I — 2025_AUGUST* for cavernous sinus thrombosis and arteriovenous fistula.
* **Diagram Reference:** [Cavernous Sinus Schematic (Wikimedia Commons)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/Cavernous_Sinus_Schematic.jpg)

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Rectus Abdominis Muscle
notes.content:
* **Origin:** Lateral head from pubic crest; medial head from anterior pubic symphysis.
* **Insertion:** Costal cartilages of 5th, 6th, and 7th ribs; xiphoid process.
* **Characteristics:** Traversed by 3 tendinous intersections (intersectio tendinea) adhering to the anterior rectus sheath.
* **Nerve Supply:** Anterior rami of lower six thoracic nerves (**T7–T12**).
* **Actions:** Flexes lumbar spine; compresses abdominal viscera; increases intra-abdominal pressure.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Development and Congenital Anomalies of Palate
notes.questionText: Describe the development and congenital anomalies of palate
notes.content:
* **Development:**
  1. **Primary Palate:** Formed by the inward growth and fusion of the two **medial nasal processes** (forms premaxilla carrying upper 4 incisors).
  2. **Secondary Palate:** Formed from bilateral **palatal processes (shelves)** growing inward from the maxillary prominences. In the 7th–8th week, the shelves elevate above the descending tongue and fuse with each other and with the downward-growing nasal septum.
  3. Fusion proceeds from anterior to posterior, ending with the uvula in the 11th week.
* **Congenital Anomalies:**
  * *Cleft Uvula:* Mildest form; failure of uvular tips to fuse.
  * *Unilateral Cleft Palate:* Failure of one lateral palatine shelf to fuse with the primary palate and nasal septum.
  * *Bilateral Complete Cleft Palate:* Complete failure of both palatal shelves to fuse; leaves large cleft communicating with nasal cavity.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Cerebrum Superolateral Surface — Sulci, Gyri, Functional Areas, and Blood Supply
notes.questionText: Describe the Sulci, Gyri, functional areas and blood supply on the superolateral surface of cerebrum
notes.content:
* **Major Sulci:** Lateral sulcus (of Sylvius), Central sulcus (of Rolando), Parieto-occipital sulcus.
* **Lobes and Major Functional Areas:**
  * *Frontal Lobe:*
    * **Primary Motor Area (Area 4):** In precentral gyrus; initiates voluntary motor movement.
    * **Premotor Area (Area 6):** Coordinates motor skills.
    * **Broca’s Motor Speech Area (Areas 44, 45):** In pars triangularis/opercularis of dominant hemisphere [111001:Q01].
  * *Parietal Lobe:*
    * **Primary Somatosensory Area (Areas 3, 1, 2):** In postcentral gyrus.
    * **Wernicke’s Sensory Speech Area (Area 22, 39, 40):** Receptive language comprehension [102001:Q04].
  * *Temporal Lobe:*
    * **Primary Auditory Area (Areas 41, 42):** In superior temporal gyrus (Heschl’s gyri).
  * *Occipital Lobe:*
    * **Primary Visual Area (Area 17):** In occipital pole / calcarine banks [102001:Q04].
* **Blood Supply:** Supplied mainly by the **Middle Cerebral Artery (MCA)**, except an upper $1\text{ inch}$ strip supplied by ACA and occipital/inferotemporal margins supplied by PCA [102001:Q04].

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Microscopic Structure of Small Intestine
notes.questionText: Explain the microscopic structure of small intestine
notes.content:
* **Common Architectural Layers:**
  1. **Mucosa:**
     * *Villi:* Finger-like projections lined by simple columnar enterocytes with microvillus brush border and goblet cells.
     * *Crypts of Lieberkühn:* Mucosal pits containing stem cells, **Paneth cells** (secrete antibacterial defensins/lysozyme), and enteroendocrine cells [102001:Q12].
     * *Lacteals:* Central lymphatic capillary in each villus for chylomicron absorption.
  2. **Submucosa:** Highly vascular dense connective tissue containing the Submucosal (Meissner’s) nerve plexus.
  3. **Muscularis Externa:** Inner circular and outer longitudinal smooth muscle layers with intervening Myenteric (Auerbach’s) nerve plexus.
  4. **Serosa:** Lined by simple squamous mesothelium.
* **Regional Diagnostic Differences:**
  * **Duodenum:** Presence of branched tubuloalveolar **Brunner’s Glands in the submucosa** [102001:Q12].
  * **Jejunum:** Tall, leaf-like villi, numerous plicae circulares (valves of Kerckring), no Brunner's glands, no Peyer's patches.
  * **Ileum:** Flatter villi, contains aggregated lymphoid follicles called **Peyer’s Patches** in mucosa and submucosa on the antimesenteric border.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Jugular Foramen
notes.content:
Located between the petrous temporal bone and occipital bone:
* **Anterior Part:** Transmits the **Inferior Petrosal Sinus**.
* **Intermediate (Middle) Part:** Transmits Cranial Nerves:
  1. **Glossopharyngeal Nerve (CN IX)**
  2. **Vagus Nerve (CN X)**
  3. **Accessory Nerve (CN XI)**
  4. Meningeal branch of ascending pharyngeal artery
* **Posterior Part:** Transmits termination of **Sigmoid Sinus** forming the **Internal Jugular Vein**, and emissary veins.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Ligaments of Urinary Bladder
notes.content:
* **True Ligaments (Endopelvic Fascia Condensations):**
  1. *Puboprostatic (in male) / Pubovesical (in female) Ligaments:* Anchor bladder neck to pubic bones.
  2. *Lateral True Ligaments:* Connect bladder base to lateral pelvic walls.
  3. *Median Umbilical Ligament:* Fibrous cord of obliterated **urachus** extending from apex to umbilicus [112001:Q01].
  4. *Posterior Ligaments:* Anchor base to lateral pelvic wall.
* **False Ligaments (Peritoneal Folds):** Median umbilical fold, medial umbilical folds, and sacrogenital folds.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Development of Face
notes.content:
* Develops between the 4th and 8th weeks from five mesenchymal facial swellings surrounding the stomodeum:
  1. **Frontonasal Prominence:** Forms forehead, nose bridge, medial/lateral nasal processes.
  2. **Medial Nasal Processes (paired):** Fuse in midline to form philtrum of upper lip, premaxilla, and primary palate.
  3. **Lateral Nasal Processes (paired):** Form alae of nose.
  4. **Maxillary Prominences (paired):** Form cheeks, lateral upper lip, and secondary palate.
  5. **Mandibular Prominences (paired):** Fuse in midline to form lower lip and jaw.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Tonsillectomy Nerve Injury, Tongue Anatomy, and Tonsil Histology
notes.questionText: A 10-year-old girl underwent bilateral tonsillectomy for chronic tonsillitis. On examination, prior to discharge, the surgeon noted an absence of touch sensation on the posterior ⅓ of the tongue along with an absent gag reflex. Based on your knowledge of anatomy answer the following questions: a) Name the nerve damaged during the surgery b) What are the external features on the posterior ⅓ of tongue c) Correlate the development of the tongue to its nerve supply d) Briefly describe the histology of the tonsil (1+2+4+3)
notes.content:
##### a) Nerve Damaged During Surgery
* **Glossopharyngeal Nerve (CN IX):** Runs directly in the muscular bed of the palatine tonsil intimate to stylopharyngeus and middle pharyngeal constrictor.

##### b) External Features on Posterior One-Third of Tongue
* Lacks true lingual papillae; surface is irregular and nodular due to underlying submucosal lymphoid aggregations called the **Lingual Tonsil**.
* Separated from the anterior two-thirds by the V-shaped **Sulcus Terminalis**, at the apex of which lies the **Foramen Cecum** [102001:Q10].
* Mucosa is reflected posteriorly onto the epiglottis, forming the median glossoepiglottic fold and bilateral lateral glossoepiglottic folds flanking the **Valleculae**.

##### c) Development of Tongue Correlated with Nerve Supply
* **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:102001:Q10]]` under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2026_JANUARY* for 1st arch (Lingual V3 and Chorda Tympani VII), 3rd arch hypobranchial eminence (Glossopharyngeal IX), 4th arch (Internal Laryngeal X), and occipital myotomes (Hypoglossal XII).

##### d) Histology of Palatine Tonsil
* **Epithelium:** Covered by **stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium** which invaginates deeply into underlying lymphoid tissue forming 10–20 blind-ended **Tonsillar Crypts**.
* **Lymphoid Tissue:** Dense masses of spherical **lymphatic nodules (follicles)** with prominent pale germinal centers.
* **Hemicapsule:** A distinct fibrous connective tissue band shields the deep aspect, separating the tonsil from the pharyngeal musculature and facilitating surgical dissection. Devoid of subcapsular and lymph sinuses (no afferent lymphatics; possesses only efferent channels).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Neurulation and Brain Vesicles Fate
notes.questionText: Describe the process of neurulation. Name the vesicles in the cranial expanded part of the neural tube and mention their fate. (4+2)
notes.content:
* **Process of Neurulation:**
  1. In the 3rd week, the notochord induces overlying surface ectoderm to thicken into the **neural plate** [111001:Q01].
  2. Neural plate invaginates along midline, producing a **neural groove** flanked by elevated **neural folds**.
  3. Folds converge and fuse in the midline in the 4th week, beginning at the 4th somite level and progressing cranially and caudally to form the **neural tube**.
  4. Temporary openings remain: **Anterior Neuropore** (closes day 25) and **Posterior Neuropore** (closes day 28). Neural crest cells detach from the lateral margins [111001:Q01].
* **Primary Brain Vesicles (Cranial Expanded End) and Fate:**
  1. **Prosencephalon (Forebrain):**
     * *Telencephalon:* Forms cerebral hemispheres, basal nuclei, and lateral ventricles [111001:Q01, 111001:Q08].
     * *Diencephalon:* Forms thalamus, hypothalamus, epithalamus, and third ventricle [112001:Q19].
  2. **Mesencephalon (Midbrain):** Forms midbrain (tectum, red nucleus, substantia nigra, crus cerebri) and cerebral aqueduct [111001:Q19].
  3. **Rhombencephalon (Hindbrain):**
     * *Metencephalon:* Forms pons, cerebellum, and upper 4th ventricle.
     * *Myelencephalon:* Forms medulla oblongata and lower 4th ventricle.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Chromosome Structure, Classification, and Three Structural Anomalies
notes.questionText: Describe the structure of chromosomes with classification. Explain any three structural anomalies of chromosomes (4+2)
notes.content:
* **Chromosome Structure:** Composed of chromatin (DNA double helix wrapped around histone octamers forming nucleosomes); contains two sister chromatids joined at a primary constriction (**centromere / kinetochore**) with short ($p$) and long ($q$) arms and terminal protective **telomeres**.
* **Morphological Classification (Centromeric Position):**
  1. *Metacentric:* Centromere in middle; $p$ and $q$ arms equal.
  2. *Submetacentric:* Centromere displaced off-center; short $p$ arm and longer $q$ arm.
  3. *Acrocentric:* Centromere located near one end; possesses satellite stalks (chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 21, 22).
  4. *Telocentric:* Centromere at terminal end (not present in normal human karyotype).
* **Three Structural Anomalies:**
  1. **Translocation:** Transfer of genetic material between non-homologous chromosomes (e.g., *Robertsonian translocation* between acrocentric chromosomes, or reciprocal translocation $t(9;22)$).
  2. **Deletion:** Loss of a chromosomal segment (e.g., *Cri-du-chat syndrome* caused by $5p-$ deletion).
  3. **Inversion:** A two-break segment rotates $180^\circ$ and reinserts (paracentric if excluding centromere, pericentric if including centromere).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Implantation and Common Abnormal Sites
notes.questionText: Describe the process of implantation and common abnormal sites of implantation (3+3)
notes.content:
* **Process of Implantation:**
  1. The blastocyst hatches from the *zona pellucida* on day 6 [101001:Q05].
  2. On day 7, the embryonic pole trophoblast adheres to the uterine endometrial epithelium (secretory phase endometrium).
  3. Trophoblast differentiates into inner **cytotrophoblast** and outer invasive multinucleated **syncytiotrophoblast** which secretes metalloproteinases.
  4. Syncytiotrophoblast erodes maternal capillaries and endometrial glands, embedding blastocyst completely within the stroma by day 10–11 (interstitial implantation). Defect sealed by closing coagulum.
* **Abnormal Implantation Sites (Ectopic Pregnancy):**
  * *Tubal (95%):* Ampulla (most common) [111001:Q01], isthmus, or fimbrial end.
  * *Ovarian:* Implantation within the ovary.
  * *Abdominal (Peritoneal):* Pouch of Douglas or mesentery.
  * *Cervical:* Lower cervix.
  * *Placenta Previa:* Implantation in lower uterine segment near the internal os.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Transitional Epithelium (Urothelium)
notes.content:
* **Location:** Renal calyces, renal pelvis, ureters, urinary bladder [111001:Q01, 111001:Q05], prostatic urethra.
* **Microscopic Characteristics:**
  * Multilayered (4–6 layers) specialized stratified epithelium capable of distension.
  * *Basal Layer:* Small cuboidal/columnar cells resting on delicate basement membrane.
  * *Intermediate Layers:* Polyhedral cells with pyriform (pear-shaped) morphology.
  * *Superficial Layer:* Large, umbrella-shaped facet cells (often binucleated) featuring apical cytoplasmic condensations (**uroplakin plaques**) providing an impermeable osmotic barrier against hypertonic urine.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Layers of Scalp, Bleeding, and Dangerous Layer
notes.questionText: Name the layers of the scalp. Why do scalp wounds bleed profusely. Which layer is considered the dangerous layer and why (2+2+2)
notes.content:
* **Layers of Scalp (Mnemonic: SCALP):**
  1. **S** – **Skin:** Thick, dense, containing abundant hair follicles and sebaceous glands.
  2. **C** – **Connective Tissue (Dense Subcutaneous):** Richly vascular, inelastic fibrous septa tether skin to underlying aponeurosis.
  3. **A** – **Aponeurosis (Galea Aponeurotica):** Tough tendon connecting frontalis and occipitalis muscles.
  4. **L** – **Loose Areolar Tissue:** Creates a potential cleavage plane.
  5. **P** – **Pericranium:** External periosteum of cranial vault bones.
* **Why Scalp Wounds Bleed Profusely:** Scalp blood vessels run within Layer 2 (dense connective tissue) anchored to tough collagenous septa. When severed, the cut vessels **cannot retract or contract**, remaining held wide open, producing severe, continuous arterial hemorrhage [111001:Q01].
* **Dangerous Layer of Scalp:** **Layer 4 (Loose Areolar Tissue)**:
  * Contains valve-less **emissary veins** connecting scalp veins directly with intracranial dural venous sinuses.
  * Pus or infected hematoma within this layer can spread easily through emissary veins, causing **cavernous sinus thrombosis** or meningitis [111001:Q17].
  * Blood can track forward into the eyelids (producing "black eye") because the frontalis muscle lacks bony insertion.

notes.title: Karyotype and Clinical Features of Klinefelter Syndrome

notes.content:

  * Testicular atrophy and hypogonadism (small, firm testes lacking spermatogenesis; primary infertility).
  * **Gynecomastia** (increased risk of breast carcinoma).
  * High-pitched voice, sparse facial and body hair.
  * Barr body positive (1 Barr body) [101001:Q05].

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Anatomical Basis of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
notes.questionText: Explain the anatomical basis of carpal tunnel syndrome
notes.content:
* **Compressive Pathology:** Entrapment neuropathy of the **Median Nerve** inside the osteofibrous **carpal tunnel** beneath the rigid **flexor retinaculum** [101001:Q11, 111001:Q01].
* **Precipitating Factors:** Synovial tenosynovitis of flexor tendons, fluid retention (pregnancy, myxedema), rheumatoid arthritis, or distal radius fracture (Colles' fracture).
* **Clinical Presentation:**
  * Paresthesia, burning pain, and numbness over the palmar surface of the lateral $3\frac{1}{2}$ digits.
  * *Thenar Atrophy:* Weakness and flattening of thenar eminence due to loss of motor supply to the **abductor pollicis brevis**, **flexor pollicis brevis**, and **opponens pollicis** ("ape-thumb deformity") [111001:Q01].
  * Preservation of palmar sensation over central palm (because the *palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve* passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Annular Pancreas Case and Pancreas Anatomy
notes.questionText: During an abdominal surgery, the doctor observed a ring of pancreatic tissue surrounding the duodenum and obstructing it. Describe pancreas under a) Gross features b) Relations, c) Development d) Microscopic structure (2+4+2+2)
notes.content:
##### a) Gross Features
* Soft, lobulated, retroperitoneal organ ($12–15\text{ cm}$ long) lying transversely across the posterior abdominal wall from the C-loop of the duodenum to the spleen.
* **Parts:** Head (lodged in duodenal loop, possesses uncinate process), Neck (overlies superior mesenteric vessels), Body (prismatic, 3 surfaces: anterior, posterior, inferior), and Tail (narrow mobile extremity in lienorenal ligament touching splenic hilum).

##### b) Relations
* **Anterior:** Transverse colon, transverse mesocolon, stomach (separated by lesser sac) [102001:Q01].
* **Posterior:** Inferior Vena Cava, Left Renal Vein, Abdominal Aorta, Superior Mesenteric Artery, Left Crus of Diaphragm, Left Kidney and Suprarenal Gland, and Splenic Vein (runs embedded in a posterior groove).

##### c) Development and Annular Pancreas
* **Development:**
  * **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:102001:Q10]]` under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2026_JUNE* for ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds and duct formation.
* **Annular Pancreas:** Caused by the **bifid ventral pancreatic bud**. The two components migrate in opposite directions around the 2nd part of the duodenum, fusing with the dorsal bud to form a complete encircling collar of pancreatic tissue, causing **duodenal stenosis/atresia** presenting with non-bilious/bilious vomiting in the newborn [112001:Q01].

##### d) Microscopic Structure
* **Exocrine Part (98–99%):** Pure serous tubuloacinar glands. Acinar cells are pyramidal with basal basophilic cytoplasm (rough ER) and apical acidophilic **zymogen granules**. Distinctive **Centroacinar cells** (pale duct cells projecting into the acinar lumen) line intercalated ducts; lacks striated ducts.
* **Endocrine Part (1–2% - Islets of Langerhans):** Spherical, pale-staining clusters of polygonal endocrine cells surrounded by fenestrated capillaries:
  * *Beta cells (70%):* Synthesize Insulin.
  * *Alpha cells (20%):* Synthesize Glucagon.
  * *Delta cells (5–10%):* Synthesize Somatostatin.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Case — Diaphragm Anatomy
notes.questionText: A 23year-old pregnant woman who did not go for regular antenatal screening delivered a full-term baby weighing 2kg. Soon after birth the baby was found to be dyspnoeic and vomited continuously after every feed. CT was done for the newborn and it revealed herniation of stomach and intestines into the left side of thoracic cavity. With your knowledge in anatomy, answer the following: a) Name the structure that is defectively developed in this newborn. b) Describe the attachments of this structure. c) Mention the innervation and actions of this structure. d) Mention the openings in this structure and structures passing through them. e) Describe the development of this structure. (1+2+2+3+2)
notes.content:
##### a) Defectively Developed Structure
* **Thoracoabdominal Diaphragm** (specifically failure of fusion of the **Pleuroperitoneal Membrane**, causing **Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia of Bochdalek** on the left side) [112001:Q17].

##### b) Attachments of Diaphragm
* Dome-shaped musculotendinous partition possessing peripheral origins inserting into a **Central Tendon**:
  1. *Sternal Origin:* Two small muscular slips from the posterior surface of the xiphoid process.
  2. *Costal Origin:* Inner surfaces of lower 6 costal cartilages and adjacent ribs (interdigitating with transversus abdominis).
  3. *Vertebral / Lumbar Origin:*
     * **Right Crus:** Arises from anterolateral bodies of upper 3 lumbar vertebrae (L1–L3).
     * **Left Crus:** Arises from anterolateral bodies of upper 2 lumbar vertebrae (L1–L2).
     * **Arcuate Ligaments:** Medial arcuate ligament (thickening of psoas fascia) and Lateral arcuate ligament (thickening of quadratus lumborum fascia).
* *Insertion:* Trifoliate **Central Tendon of the Diaphragm**.

##### c) Innervation and Actions
* **Innervation:**
  * Motor: **Phrenic Nerve (C3, C4, C5)** [112001:Q01].
  * Sensory: Phrenic nerve supplies the central tendon and mediastinal/diaphragmatic pleura/peritoneum; lower 6 intercostal nerves supply peripheral margins [112001:Q16].
* **Actions:**
  * Primary muscle of inspiration: Contraction pulls the central tendon downward, flattening domes, increasing vertical thoracic volume and creating negative intrathoracic pressure.
  * Muscle of abdominal straining: Increases intra-abdominal pressure during micturition, defecation, and parturition.

##### d) Openings and Transmitted Structures
* **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:112001:Q17]]` under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2025_NOVEMBER* for T8 caval, T10 esophageal, and T12 aortic openings.

##### e) Development of Diaphragm
* **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:112001:Q17]]` under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2025_NOVEMBER* for Septum Transversum, Pleuroperitoneal membranes, Dorsal mesentery of esophagus, and Body wall mesenchyme.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Sciatic Nerve
notes.questionText: Describe sciatic nerve under following headings: root value, course and relations, branches and clinical anatomy. (1+4+3+2)
notes.content:
* **Root Value:** Arises from ventral and dorsal divisions of ventral rami of **L4, L5, S1, S2, S3** (Sacral Plexus).
* **Course and Relations:**
  * Enters the gluteal region through the **greater sciatic foramen** below the piriformis muscle.
  * Descends midway between the ischial tuberosity and greater trochanter of the femur.
  * Rests anteriorly upon the ischium, superior gemellus, obturator internus, inferior gemellus, quadratus femoris, and adductor magnus.
  * Covered posteriorly by the Gluteus Maximus, then crossed obliquely by the long head of the Biceps Femoris in the middle third of the thigh.
  * Terminates at the superior angle of the **popliteal fossa** by dividing into:
    1. **Tibial Nerve**
    2. **Common Peroneal Nerve** [101001:Q03]
* **Branches:**
  * *Articular:* Branches to hip joint.
  * *Muscular:* To hamstring muscles (Semitendinosus, Semimembranosus, Long head of Biceps femoris, Ischial part of adductor magnus via tibial component; Short head of Biceps femoris via common peroneal component) [112001:Q21].
* **Clinical Anatomy:**
  * *Sciatica:* Shooting, burning pain radiating down the posterior thigh and lateral/posterior leg along the sciatic distribution, commonly caused by lumbar disc herniation (L4–L5 or L5–S1) compressing nerve roots.
  * *Intramuscular Injections:* Must be administered exclusively in the **upper outer quadrant of the gluteal region** to avoid impaling the sciatic nerve.
  * *Posterior Dislocation of Hip:* Stretches or lacerates the nerve [112001:Q16].
* **Diagram Reference:** [Sciatic Nerve Distribution (Wikimedia Commons)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/da/Sciatic_nerve2.jpg)

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Boundaries and Contents of Ischiorectal Fossa
notes.questionText: Boundaries and contents of ischiorectal fossa
notes.content:
* **Boundaries:**
  * *Base (Inferior):* Perianal skin and superficial fascia.
  * *Apex (Superior):* Meeting of obturator and anal fascias at the origin of levator ani.
  * *Medial Wall:* Sloping **Levator Ani** and **External Anal Sphincter** covered by anal fascia.
  * *Lateral Wall:* **Obturator Internus** muscle covered by obturator fascia and ischial tuberosity.
  * *Anterior:* Posterior border of the perineal membrane.
  * *Posterior:* Sacrotuberous ligament and lower border of Gluteus Maximus.
* **Contents:**
  1. **Ischiorectal Fat Pad:** Shock-absorbing, soft adipose tissue allowing distension of anal canal during defecation.
  2. **Pudendal (Alcock’s) Canal:** Fascial tunnel on the lateral wall transmitting the **Internal Pudendal Vessels** and **Pudendal Nerve**.
  3. **Inferior Rectal Nerves and Vessels:** Branch across the fossa to supply the lower anal canal and sphincter [112001:Q09, 112001:Q12].
  4. Scrotal/labial nerves and perineal branch of S4.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Histology of Pituitary Gland (Hypophysis Cerebri)
notes.content:
* **Adenohypophysis (Anterior Pituitary - derived from Rathke’s pouch):**
  1. *Pars Distalis:* Cords of secretory cells supported by reticular stroma and fenestrated sinusoidal capillaries:
     * **Chromophobes (50%):** Pale, degranulated non-staining resting cells.
     * **Chromophils (50%):**
       * *Acidophils (40%):* Stain pink/red; secrete **Growth Hormone (GH)** (somatotropes) and **Prolactin** (mammotropes).
       * *Basophils (10%):* Stain blue; secrete **ACTH**, **TSH**, **FSH**, and **LH**.
  2. *Pars Intermedia:* Contains colloid-filled cysts (Rathke’s cysts); secretes MSH.
* **Neurohypophysis (Posterior Pituitary - derived from diencephalon neuroectoderm):**
  * Consists of unmyelinated hypothalamic axons from supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
  * **Herring Bodies:** Eosinophilic neurosecretory axon swellings containing **Oxytocin** and **Vasopressin (ADH)**.
  * **Pituicytes:** Specialized glial support cells.

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Development of Kidney and Associated Anomalies
notes.questionText: Describe the development of kidney and its associated anomalies. (4+2)
notes.content:
* **Embryological Sources:**
  1. **Ureteric Bud:** Outgrowth of the mesonephric duct [112001:Q01]; gives rise to the **collecting system**: ureter, renal pelvis, major and minor calyces, and $1–3\text{ million}$ collecting tubules [112001:Q01].
  2. **Metanephric Blastema (Mesoderm):** Condensation of intermediate mesoderm; gives rise to the **excretory units (nephrons)**: Bowman’s capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, and DCT.
* **Ascent and Rotation:** Ascends from the sacral region to lumbar site; rotates $90^\circ$ medially so the hilum points medially.
* **Congenital Anomalies:**
  * **Horseshoe Kidney:** Lower poles fuse across the midline; ascent is arrested when trapped beneath the **Inferior Mesenteric Artery (L3)**.
  * **Polycystic Kidney Disease (Autosomal Recessive/Dominant):** Failure of developing nephrons to properly interconnect with collecting tubules, producing massive cystic dilation and renal failure.
  * **Renal Agenesis:** Bilateral agenesis leads to oligohydramnios and Potter sequence.
  * **Pelvic Kidney / Ectopic Kidney:** Failure of ascent.

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Microscopic Features of Fundus and Pyloric Part of Stomach
notes.questionText: Describe the microscopic features of fundus and pyloric part of stomach. (3+3)
notes.content:
| Histological Feature | Fundus of Stomach | Pyloric Part of Stomach |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gastric Pits (Foveolae)** | Shallow, narrow pits occupying $\approx \frac{1}{4}$ of mucosal thickness | Deep, branched pits occupying $\frac{1}{2}$ or more of mucosal thickness |
| **Gastric Glands** | Simple straight tubular glands packed closely together | Branched, coiled, tortuous tubular glands with wide lumina |
| **Parietal (Oxyntic) Cells** | **Abundant**; large triangular/pyramidal eosinophilic cells secreting **$HCl$** and **Intrinsic Factor** | Very few or completely absent |
| **Chief (Peptic) Cells** | **Abundant**; basophilic base, secretes **Pepsinogen** | Sparse or absent |
| **Mucous / Enteroendocrine Cells**| Few neck cells | Predominated by **mucus-secreting cells** and **G-cells** secreting **Gastrin** |
| **Muscularis Externa** | Inner oblique, middle circular, outer longitudinal | Massive thickening of middle circular layer forming **Pyloric Sphincter** [102001:Q01] |

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Coverings and Blood Supply of Spinal Cord
notes.questionText: Coverings and blood supply of spinal cord
notes.content:
* **Meninges (Coverings):**
  1. *Dura Mater:* Tough, fibrous outermost tubular sheath extending to **S2** [111001:Q01].
  2. *Arachnoid Mater:* Avascular translucent membrane; subarachnoid space filled with CSF.
  3. *Pia Mater:* Vascular innermost membrane adhering to spinal cord; gives off lateral tooth-like **ligamenta denticulata** (21 pairs) anchoring cord to dura.
* **Arterial Supply:**
  * **One Anterior Spinal Artery:** Formed by union of vertebral branches; runs in anterior median fissure; supplies anterior two-thirds of cord.
  * **Two Posterior Spinal Arteries:** Arise from vertebral or PICA; run along posterolateral sulci.
  * **Radicular Arteries:** Enter via intervertebral foramina; largest is the **Arteria Radicularis Magna (of Adamkiewicz)** arising from lower intercostal/lumbar aorta (supplies lumbosacral cord).

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Muscles of Soft Palate with Nerve Supply
notes.questionText: Muscles of soft palate with nerve supply
notes.content:
| Muscle | Origin | Insertion | Nerve Supply | Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tensor Veli Palatini** | Scaphoid fossa of sphenoid, spine of sphenoid, auditory tube | Palatine aponeurosis (hooks around pterygoid hamulus) | **Nerve to Medial Pterygoid** (Mandibular nerve, V3) | Tenses soft palate; opens auditory tube |
| **Levator Veli Palatini** | Petrous temporal bone & auditory tube | Palatine aponeurosis | Cranial Accessory (CN XI) via pharyngeal plexus | Elevates soft palate |
| **Palatoglossus** | Palatine aponeurosis | Side of tongue | Cranial Accessory (CN XI) via pharyngeal plexus [102001:Q10] | Elevates root of tongue; narrows oropharyngeal isthmus |
| **Palatopharyngeus** | Palatine aponeurosis | Posterior border of thyroid cartilage | Cranial Accessory (CN XI) via pharyngeal plexus | Elevates pharynx and larynx |
| **Musculus Uvulae** | Posterior nasal spine | Mucous membrane of uvula | Cranial Accessory (CN XI) via pharyngeal plexus | Shortens and elevates uvula |

* *Rule:* All soft palate muscles are supplied by **CN XI via pharyngeal plexus**, **EXCEPT Tensor Veli Palatini** (supplied by **V3**).

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Urinary Bladder — Presenting Parts, Interior, and Microscopic Structure
notes.questionText: Describe the presenting parts, interior, microscopic structure of urinary bladder. (2+2+2)
notes.content:
* **Presenting Parts:**
  * *Apex:* Points forward toward symphysis pubis; anchored to umbilicus by the median umbilical ligament (urachus) [112001:Q09].
  * *Base (Fundus):* Triangular posterior surface related to rectum in males and vagina/uterus in females [102001:Q01, 102001:Q03].
  * *Neck:* Most dependent and fixed part; surrounds the internal urethral meatus, resting on the prostate in males [112001:Q01, 112001:Q19].
  * *Surfaces:* Superior surface (peritoneal) and two inferolateral surfaces.
* **Interior of Bladder:**
  * **REFER TO:** `[[KUHS-QUESTION:102001:Q09]]` under *Anatomy — Paper II — 2025_JANUARY* for trigone, interureteric bar, ureteric orifices, and uvula vesicae.
* **Microscopic Structure:**
  1. *Mucosa:* Lined by **Transitional Epithelium (Urothelium)** [111001:Q01, 111001:Q05, 101001:Q09] (umbrella cells with thick luminal plaques protecting against urea).
  2. *Lamina Propria:* Dense fibroelastic connective tissue (lacks muscularis mucosae).
  3. *Muscularis (Detrusor Muscle):* Three thick interlacing plexiform layers of smooth muscle (inner longitudinal, middle circular, outer longitudinal).
  4. *Adventitia / Serosa:* Serosa over superior surface; fibroareolar adventitia elsewhere.

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Nerve Supply of Tongue
notes.content:
* **Motor:** All muscles (intrinsic and extrinsic) are supplied by the **Hypoglossal Nerve (CN XII)**, **EXCEPT Palatoglossus** (supplied by Cranial Accessory via pharyngeal plexus) [102001:Q10].
* **Sensory:**
  * *Anterior Two-Thirds:* General sensation by **Lingual Nerve** (V3); Taste sensation by **Chorda Tympani** (CN VII) [102001:Q10, 111001:Q02].
  * *Posterior One-Third:* Both general and taste sensations by the **Glossopharyngeal Nerve (CN IX)** [102001:Q10, 111001:Q02].
  * *Posterior-most (Vallecula):* **Internal Laryngeal Nerve** (Vagus, CN X) [102001:Q10].

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Anatomical Basis of Femoral Hernia
notes.questionText: Describe the anatomical basis of femoral hernia.
notes.content:
* **Passage:** Protrusion of abdominal contents through the **femoral ring** into the **femoral canal** [101001:Q04].
* **Boundaries of Femoral Ring (Rigid and Unyielding):**
  * *Anterior:* Inguinal ligament.
  * *Medial:* Sharp crescentic free margin of the **Lacunar Ligament (of Gimbernat)**.
  * *Posterior:* Pectineal ligament (of Cooper) and pectineus muscle.
  * *Lateral:* Femoral Vein (separated by fibrous septum).
* **Clinical Vulnerability:**
  * More common in multiparous females due to wider female pelvis and larger femoral canal.
  * Because the femoral ring is surrounded by rigid, sharp fibrous margins (especially the lacunar ligament medially), **femoral hernias have a high incidence of irreducible strangulation and gangrene**.
  * Emergency surgical reduction requires incising the lacunar ligament medially (watching out for an anomalous obturator artery in 30%).

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Structures Passing Through Foramen Magnum
notes.content:
* **Through Narrow Anterior Compartment (Apical ligament compartment):**
  1. Apical ligament of dens
  2. Vertical band of cruciate ligament
  3. Membrana tectoria
* **Through Wide Posterior (Neurovascular) Compartment:**
  1. **Lower end of Medulla Oblongata** and meninges
  2. **Vertebral Arteries** (paired) with sympathetic plexuses
  3. **Spinal Accessory Nerves (CN XI)** (ascending spinal roots)
  4. Anterior and Posterior Spinal Arteries
  5. Tonsils of cerebellum (in Chiari malformations/herniations)

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Intercostal Muscles
notes.content:
* **Three Layers:**
  1. **External Intercostal Muscle (11 pairs):** Fibers directed downwards and forwards ("hands in pockets"); extends from the rib tubercles behind to the costochondral junctions in front, continuing as the *anterior intercostal membrane*. Elevates ribs in inspiration.
  2. **Internal Intercostal Muscle (11 pairs):** Fibers run downwards and backwards; extends from sternum anteriorly to rib angles posteriorly, continuing as the *posterior intercostal membrane*. Depresses ribs in forced expiration.
  3. **Innermost Intercostal Muscle:** Subdivided into *subcostalis*, *intercostalis intimus*, and *transversus thoracis (sternocostalis)*. Separated from internal intercostal by the intercostal neurovascular bundle (**Vein, Artery, Nerve** from above down) [101001:Q09, 112001:Q01].
* **Innervation:** Intercostal nerves of the corresponding space.

---

notes.subject: Anatomy
notes.title: Factors Stabilizing the Ankle Joint
notes.questionText: Describe the factors stabilizing the ankle joint.
notes.content:
* **Type of Joint:** Synovial Hinge Joint (Talocrural joint) [101001:Q06].
* **Stabilizing Factors:**
  1. **Bony Architecture (Mortise-and-Tenon Fit):** Deep, rigid socket formed by the inferior articular surface of the tibia, medial malleolus, and lateral malleolus gripping the wedge-shaped trochlea of the talus. Most stable in **dorsiflexion** (wider anterior trochlea wedges tightly into socket).
  2. **Collateral Ligaments:**
     * *Deltoid Ligament (Medial Collateral):* Extremely powerful, triangular ligament (tibionavicular, tibiocalcaneal, anterior and posterior tibiotalar parts); prevents eversion dislocation.
     * *Lateral Collateral Ligament:* Weaker; composed of three distinct bands: Anterior Talofibular Ligament (ATFL, most frequently torn in inversion sprains), Calcaneofibular Ligament, and Posterior Talofibular Ligament.
  3. **Inferior Tibiofibular Syndesmosis:** Strong interosseous tibiofibular ligament and transverse tibiofibular ligament maintaining cohesion of the mortise.
  4. **Dynamic Muscle Tendons:** Tendons of Tibialis anterior, Extensor hallucis longus, Extensor digitorum longus crossing anteriorly; Tendo Achilles posteriorly; Peronei laterally; Tibialis posterior, FDL, FHL medially.
